_comment: PROVIDER PLUG-IN for the `shariah-governance` role — the external alternative, for institutions that run ISSC papers, resolutions and sign-offs through a GRC or Shari'ah-workflow platform rather than a secretariat share. It exists so the role is a genuine choice and not one arrangement with extra steps; the role's demand does not soften either way. What changes is WHO asserts the register: a platform outside the repository, whose resolution and approval records carry its own timestamps and audit trail. It still rules on nothing — scholars decide Shari'ah, the platform records that they did. To adopt: record the choice in docs/governance/provider-selection.json, copy this file to docs/governance/adapters/, point it at your tenant, and wire the fetch that fills activation_evidence.
capability: The ISSC arrangement as the workflow platform holds it — committee membership with HSA approval and appointment references, sitting minutes, and the resolution record behind each ruling — read from the platform's API, not from the repository under test

role_fit._comment: Stated plainly so the choice is made with open eyes, not sold. Neither line is a reason to prefer or avoid this provider — they are the trade the institution is accepting.
role_fit.strength: The assertion comes from OUTSIDE the repository by construction: membership changes are workflow events with platform-side timestamps, so a seat cannot appear in the register without appearing in an audit trail no repository edit can rewrite. The separation the in-house route has to manufacture is the platform's default state
role_fit.limitation: The platform knows what was ENTERED into it, not what the committee decided in the room. A resolution the secretariat mis-keys reconciles perfectly and is still wrong, so the minutes reference — not the workflow state — is what an auditor follows. Two further consequences to accept deliberately: ISSC papers in a third-party tenant is a residency and confidentiality decision of its own; and a platform can carry the workflow for all three lines but can hold NO role — internal Shari'ah audit may never be outsourced, so a vendor identity in the `shariah-audit` slot has not satisfied it

reconciliation._comment: Same binding as any shariah-governance provider: the register the gate reads must match the committee the platform holds, on composition and on provenance. record_last_modified is carried so a register exported before an appointment changed is visible as stale rather than read as current.

activation_evidence._comment: ADOPT: fill from a real API read against your tenant + the tamper probe. Staleness matters here in a way it does not for a secretariat export — a platform read cached from before a resignation reports a lawful committee that no longer sits.
activation_evidence.fetched_at: ADOPT: timestamp of your platform API read
activation_evidence.reader_identity: ADOPT: the least-privilege service account that reads the register — must NOT be the coding agent's identity
activation_evidence.staleness_probe: ADOPT: 'rejected' once you have tested that a register export older than your appointment-change window fails the build
activation_evidence.tamper_probe: ADOPT: 'rejected' once you have tested that editing docs/governance/issc-register.json away from the platform's record fails the build
